edges.description: Too few mature oligodendrocytes are generated to lay down CNS myelin.
The myelin deficit is what MRI detects as diffuse hypomyelination.
Deficient myelination of the callosal fibres thins the corpus callosum.
The authors relate the hypomyelination to the spastic/dystonic quadriplegia and nystagmus.
Global delay accompanies the hypomyelination in every reported patient; the link is the general one for hypomyelinating leukodystrophies and is not separately demonstrated for HIKESHI.
Proposed by the case-series authors; inferred from cell biology and the clinical association with fever, not demonstrated in patients.

The founding report's alternative hypothesis for the fever-associated deaths: nuclear HSP70 actively protects stressed cells, so cells that cannot import it are left unprotected. The authors' main hypothesis is the extra-nuclear HSP70 immune path, modelled as a competing node. The proximate cause of death is unknown.
Fever imposes the heat stress that HIKESHI-deficient cells cannot buffer. Shown as an abnormal heat-shock response in patient iPSCs at a febrile-range temperature; not demonstrated in patients.

nodes.description: Biallelic HIKESHI missense variants leave little or no HIKESHI protein. HIKESHI is undetectable in fibroblasts homozygous for p.(Val54Leu), p.(Cys4Ser) or p.(Phe2Val), and patient iPSCs have markedly reduced HIKESHI after heat shock. Structural modelling places p.(Cys4Ser) and p.(Val54Leu) in the hydrophobic pockets of the N-terminal domain of the asymmetric homodimer, where they destabilise the protein. Proteasome inhibition partly restores the mutant protein in patient-derived cells, consistent with proteasomal degradation of an unstable protein. The activity lost is HIKESHI's own: binding the ATP form of HSP70 and carrying it through the nuclear pore.

nodes.description: Emerging, untested hypothesis from the founding report. No study has measured extra-nuclear HSP70, cytokines or natural-killer-cell activity in patients.

HIKESHI is the carrier for nuclear import of the HSP70 chaperones (HSPA1A/HSPA1B/HSPA8). It binds FG-nucleoporins and translocates through the nuclear pore on its own, carrying the ATP form of HSP70. Its loss abolishes heat-induced nuclear accumulation of HSP70 and also lowers nuclear HSP70 in unstressed cells.
